items: List Specific Depletion Triggers: Write down exact situations, clients, or contexts that drain your energy most rapidly, going beyond vague categories like 'client work' to name scope creep, unclear briefs, or unpaid invoices specifically so you can build protections around patterns instead of treating symptoms.

Document Your Warning Signs: Record physical symptoms like headaches and disrupted sleep, emotional signals like irritation toward clients you normally like, and behavioral changes like drinking more or exercising less — these are your early warning system before full burnout hits.

Identify Boundary Erosion Contexts: Note the specific moments when healthy boundaries become flexible, such as when a client asks for a quick favor, you haven't invoiced in weeks, or you're afraid saying no will cost you a referral — the context makes erosion predictable and preventable.

Define Your Exhaustion Signature: Write a personal description of what burnout actually feels like for you — whether you go numb, angry, dissociated, or make small decisions feel impossible — this distinguishes your experience from textbook definitions and helps you recognize it faster.

Execute the 72-Hour Stabilization Protocol: Take immediate action within the next 72 hours to stop the active burnout spiral, creating actual breathing room rather than planning a long recovery you cannot disappear into as a freelancer with no employer-provided leave.

Cease After-Hours Client Communication: Stop answering non-urgent emails and messages for three days, breaking the pattern where silence feels dangerous and work expands to fill every available hour — this alone can interrupt the spiral feeding your exhaustion.

Review Unpaid Invoice Patterns: Audit your outstanding invoices and income gaps that create pressure to overwork, accept unfavorable terms, or feel like sending a bill means admitting you are still struggling — financial vulnerability actively fuels burnout cycles.

Disconnect From Validation Metrics: Step back from obsessively checking client responses, proposal outcomes, and project completions that make you feel legitimate, because this achievement-seeking behavior reinforces the overwork pattern that caused burnout in the first place.

Create Daily Energy-Protecting Rituals: Design specific daily and weekly practices like morning boundaries, scheduled breaks, or end-of-day transitions that mark clearly when work stops, replacing vague intentions with physical and temporal markers that protect your energy long-term.

Establish Automatic Work Boundaries: Build systems like calendar blocks, notification schedules, and defined working hours that enforce limits without requiring willpower each day — structure that serves you instead of requiring constant discipline to maintain.

Join Freelancer Community Rituals: Participate in regular ceremonies or group practices with other freelancers to establish shared purpose and combat the isolation that accelerates burnout, creating social connection that no amount of solo self-care can replace.

Design Prevention Infrastructure: Create documented systems like weekly boundary reviews, monthly energy audits, and quarterly protocol resets that keep you from sliding backward — sustainable recovery requires checkpoints, not just initial effort.
